The old hashes were already mismatched for these values, so the file now mixes hash formats. They are skipped by the layout test via `memos` (name not in memos), so nothing is hidden today, but a later `state-partition.py --write` would silently re-encode them. in_scope: yes — suggested direction: note in task risk list or null the two hashes in a follow-up; no change required for this task.

findings.label: I1
findings.text: ast.unparse stability is not guaranteed for every future value: my probe showed no 3.12/3.13/3.14 difference and the only 3.11 mismatch was my own probe item that doesn't parse there; unparse can change across versions (f-string quoting changed in 3.12). It is stable for all 76 module-level non-def values in rr_state/*.py today (byte-identical on 3.11/3.12/3.13/3.14, including tuples, dicts, regexes, LOCK_STALE float, no f-strings). TestValueHash pins only one literal (a call with a raw string + attribute). in_scope: no

findings.label: I2
findings.text: USAGE joins any `^usage: ` line plus indented lines, not only argparse output; in the goldens `usage:` appears only in help.txt (39 lines), so no effect outside help.txt. in_scope: no
